questions.text: If half adders and full adders are implements using gates, then for the addition of two 17 bit numbers (using minimum gates) the number of half adders and full adders required will be
questions.solution:
The least significant bit has no carry-in, so a half adder is enough there. Each of the other 16 bits needs a full adder (to add the carry).

Answer: 1, 16

questions.text: The code which uses 7 bits to represent a character is :
questions.solution:
ASCII uses 7 bits (128 characters). BCD uses 4 bits per digit, EBCDIC uses 8 bits, and Gray code is not a character code.

Answer: ASCII

questions.text: The complement of the Boolean expression [latex]A B(\bar{B} C+A C)[/latex] is
questions.solution:
By De Morgan: [latex]\overline{AB(\bar BC+AC)}=\bar A+\bar B+\overline{\bar BC+AC}[/latex]

[latex]\overline{\bar BC+AC}=(B+\bar C)(\bar A+\bar C)[/latex]

Result: [latex](\bar A+\bar B)+(B+\bar C)(\bar A+\bar C)[/latex]

Answer: Option 1

questions.text: A modulus -12 ring counter requires a minimum of
questions.solution:
A ring counter circulates a single 1, so an n flip-flop ring counter has only n states. Mod-12 needs 12 flip-flops.

Answer: 12 flip-flops

questions.text: The range of integers that can be represented by an n bit 2's complement number system is:
questions.solution:
n-bit 2's complement ranges from 100..0 (most negative) to 011..1 (most positive):

[latex]-2^{n-1}[/latex] to [latex]2^{n-1}-1[/latex]

Answer: [latex]-2^{n-1}[/latex] to [latex](2^{n-1}-1)[/latex]
